title: Severity Matrix, Branching Strategy, and Backport Orchestration for Rollbacks
creator: Ava Patel
description: Purpose: Define a clear, testable protocol for classifying severity, creating patch branches, and orchestrating backports and rollbacks across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (including LTS channels). This ticket captures the decision matrix, branching naming conventions, automated verification gates, and communications templates so on-call engineers and release owners can act consistently under pressure.
acceptance_criteria: A severity matrix (S0-S3) is published and approved by Release Engineering and SRE
Branching and tag naming conventions documented and enforced by CI lint step
Automated backport job that can land a patch to an LTS branch with a single command and produces a deployment manifest
Rollback can be executed from console or CLI within 15 minutes for P0 incidents with verified health checks
Communication templates exist for customer-facing, internal, and partner channels and are linked in the run sequence
implementation_plan: 1) Finalize severity criteria and map to actions (create branch, open PR, run backport CI). 2) Add git-ops naming rules and branch protection exceptions for emergency pins. 3) Implement ci/job 'backport-orchestrator' that accepts target branches and automates cherry-picks, compile checks, and smoke deployments. 4) Add rollout gates: unit/integration, smoke, canary (5%), full rollout. 5) Add observability flags to verify before and after state. 6) Run tabletop with SRE/Support/Product to validate timing and templates.
rollback_steps: P0 rollback fast path: (1) Declare incident and set channel #incident-redwood. (2) Owner runs: ./rw-release rollback --target-tag v<TAG> --reason <short-reason> which triggers orchestration service. (3) CI validates rollback candidate against smoke tests and applies canary immediately (5% traffic). (4) Monitor key SLOs for 10 minutes; if stable, escalate to 50% then 100% rollout. (5) Post-rollback: create follow-up RFC with root cause and mitigation. Non-P0: follow queued backport path with developer/owner review.
backport_matrix: Severity -> Backport targets mapping: S0: main + last two LTS branches (lts-v1, lts-v0) + immediate customer patches; S1: main + last LTS branch; S2: main only (backport by request); S3: no backport unless security flagged. For each target branch we record: branch name, CI job, required approvals, required smoke tests. Backport strategy: prefer automated cherry-pick; if conflicts, fallback to manual resolution with assigned resolver and a 4-hour SLA for P0.
ci_jobs: Key CI jobs to add/update: 'ci/backport-orchestrator' (cherry-pick, build, test, open PR), 'ci/rollback-verify' (post-rollback smoke/integration), 'ci/lts-release-lint' (ensures backport PR meets LTS policy), 'ci/patch-binary-build' (ensures compatibility for on-prem packages). Jobs must emit structured metadata (tags, origin PR, target branches) consumed by release console.
comms_template: Internal: [INCIDENT {id}] Short summary, impact, action taken, owner, ETA for next update. Customer-facing: short plain-language description, affected versions, temporary mitigations, expected ETA for fix or rollback. Partner ops: include full manifest of effected clusters/regions and contact escalation path. Templates saved at https://confluence.redwood/release/rollback-templates (placeholder).
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-offs considered: (1) Aggressive automated backports reduce time-to-fix but increase risk of regressions on LTS branches; we mitigate with additional smoke gates. (2) Allowing emergency direct pushes to LTS shortens resolution time but weakens auditability; therefore direct pushes permitted only with two on-call approvers and full changelog. (3) Building universal binaries for all releases increases build time; mitigation: build binary only for LTS targets and rely on source-only backports for others.
